struck: Each booked night of a Myrtle Beach two-bedroom keeps about $192 after Airbnb's fee, utilities, supplies and repairs.
use: Each booked night of a Myrtle Beach two-bedroom keeps about $182 after Airbnb's fee, utilities, supplies and repairs.

struck: It needs about 105 booked nights a year to pay them, before any loan.
use: It needs about 110 booked nights a year to pay them, before any loan.

unless: part of the year|part-year|open only part
struck: The average Myrtle Beach two-bedroom books about 87 nights and keeps about $15,800 before those bills, so it falls about $4,300 short of them.
use: The average Myrtle Beach two-bedroom listing, counting listings open only part of the year, books about 87 nights and falls about $4,300 short of those bills.

struck: In Surfside Beach the bills come to about $7,600 a year, about 40 nights.
use: For condos with a Surfside Beach address the bills come to about $7,450 a year, about 42 nights.

unless: town of Surfside|inside the town|in the town
struck: The 2026 tax rate on a rental is 214.2 mills in Surfside Beach.
use: The 2026 tax rate on a rental is 214.2 mills inside the town of Surfside Beach; most condos with a Surfside Beach address sit outside the town, at 201.0.

struck: The rate is 207.3 in Garden City and the Horry side of Murrells Inlet.
use: The rate is 207.3 mills in Garden City.

struck: A nightly rental is never a legal residence, so 4 percent does not apply.
use: A legal residence rented more than 72 days a year loses the 4 percent rate.

struck: A Myrtle Beach Airbnb run by its owner keeps about 63 cents of each dollar guests pay.
use: At AirROI's low-end cost shares, an owner-run Myrtle Beach Airbnb keeps about 63 cents of each dollar guests pay.

struck: A typical July week is booked by mid-May.
use: A typical July booking is made in mid-May.

struck: 34 of 675 houses for sale in Conway are marked for nightly rentals.
use: 34 of 675 houses for sale with a Conway address are marked for nightly rentals.

struck: On the split-fee plan the host pays 3 percent and the guest pays a service fee.
use: Most hosts on the older split fee, which Airbnb is phasing out, pay 3 percent, and the guest pays a service fee.

struck: Full service costs about 40 to 60 percent.
use: Full service costs about 40 to 60 percent of gross profit, as we have seen it.

struck: On a $1,764 July week that is about $229 on top.
use: On a week at about $252 a night ($1,764), the lodging tax is about $229 on top, plus the tax on the cleaning fee.

pattern: Kings Highway[^.]{0,160}\b90 days|(cannot|can't|may not) be (rented|leased)[^.]{0,40}\b90 days
struck: Between Kings Highway and the ocean, a building of more than two units built or used for nightly stays cannot be rented for 90 days or more.
use: (cut it: Section 1808 not read; say only that Myrtle Beach adopted a short-term rental conversion overlay, Ordinance 2024-69, on December 10, 2024, and link /invest/str-rules/)

struck: The worst mistake we see is running it from another state with the cheapest cleaner.
use: The worst mistake we see is running it yourself with the cheapest cleaner.

struck: Lenders count only about 75 percent of a short-term rental estimate.
use: DSCR lenders count only about 75 percent of a short-term rental estimate, according to a loan officer at our preferred lender.
